text:
anya: quick Q — I'm updating the API contract in PR #4823. If clients omit `model` (null or empty), what is the authoritative fallback order today? I want to make sure the docs and SDKs are aligned before I merge. :thinking:

jordan: current runtime behavior is: 1) route by explicit model if present, 2) use route.hint (if set on account), 3) apply region+tier defaults configured per-customer, 4) finally fallback to our hosted default model (redwood-default-v1). But that's internal logic — we probably shouldn't guarantee all steps in the public contract. :eyes:

prateek: agree. From a backward-compat perspective, we exposed `model` as optional historically, but many integrations rely on the implicit hinting to pick cost-optimized variants. If we change order, it could break A/B rollouts. Suggestion: make the fallback order explicit in the OpenAPI docs and add an `X-Model-Resolved` response header for debugging.

liz: +1 for `X-Model-Resolved`. Also, can we standardize the `routing_params` shape clients pass? Right now we accept either `routing_policy: "region:us-west|tier:standard"` string or the object `{ region: "us-west", tier: "standard" }` — that's messy for SDKs.

anya: thanks. Proposed changes in the PR:
1) Document fallback precedence (explicit model -> account hint -> routing_params -> hosted default)
2) Normalize `routing_params` to a JSON object in the contract (legacy string still accepted for 6 months with a warning header)
3) Response header `X-Model-Resolved` added (model id used, plus a short reason code)

prateek: sounds reasonable. Can you include exact header format? e.g. `X-Model-Resolved: redwood-compact-v2;reason=hint` or `...;reason=default`

anya: yep. Draft: `X-Model-Resolved: <model-id>;reason=<explicit|hint|routing|default>`

jordan: also add `X-Model-Variant` when we apply quantized/compatible variant substitution, e.g. if a requested model isn't available in region and we pick `redwood-compact-v2-quant`. That helps perf debugging.

liz: minor but important — update the /openapi.json `required` list to not force `model`. Some auto-generated clients fail when field isn't present.

qa-bot: automated tests flagged: 2 integration tests assume implicit hint overrides routing_params. If we flip precedence in docs, we need to update those tests.

prateek: good catch. We'll keep runtime the same but call out the official precedence in docs. For safety, we should log a deprecation when `routing_policy` string format is used: `Warning: Deprecated-Routing-Policy-Format` with a 1-year deprec window.

anya: updated PR notes: added header examples + compatibility plan. Can someone from SDK/Docs review? tagging @jordan @liz. :pray:

jordan: I'll take SDKs — will ensure JavaScript/Go clients parse `routing_params` object and fall back to string for now. I'll add unit tests for `X-Model-Resolved` & `X-Model-Variant` headers.

liz: I'll update docs/openapi and add the migration guide (code snippets for both formats). Also will add a small compatibility table showing scenarios and resolved model (explicit -> same, hint only -> hint model, routing_params only -> region-based model, none -> redwood-default-v1).

prateek: from infra side, please add a short-term metric: `model_fallback.reason` tag so we can alert if we suddenly hit a surge in `default` fallback. Could mean model rollout failed.

anya: perfect. I'll patch the PR with header examples + deprecation warning text. Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge tomorrow after CI. :thumbsup:
